docs.title: Campaign Setting Query Engine
docs.text:
A knowledge graph–backed MCP server for precision lore retrieval from tabletop RPG campaign settings. Built for Eberron. Zero hallucinations — every answer cites a sourcebook page.

Canonical evaluation query: "List me the rivers of Eberron." Scored on precision + recall + F1 against ground truth extracted from the sourcebooks.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Drop in your PDF sourcebooks. The pipeline ingests them, extracts entities, and builds a SPARQL knowledge graph. Your AI agent queries it through 10 MCP tools and gets structured answers with page references — no LLM in the query path, no hallucinations.

Client / Agent
     │  MCP tools (/mcp)
     ▼
mcp-server  ──SPARQL──▶  Fuseki (OWL graph)
     │
MinIO (/raw-pdfs, /markdown)
     │
     ├── pdf-worker   (PDF → Markdown)
     └── graph-worker (Markdown → triples, LLM)

Redis  (pipeline state + entity dedup index)

docs.title: Quick links
docs.text:
• Quickstart — run locally with Docker in five minutes
  • Helm deployment — deploy to Kubernetes
  • MCP Tools — all 10 tools your agent can call
  • Admin API — ingest, status, and management endpoints
  • Configuration — every config file and environment variable
  • Ontology — entity types, properties, and SPARQL namespace

docs.title: Admin API
docs.text:
The mcp-server exposes HTTP endpoints alongside the /mcp MCP endpoint. Operators and the Streamlit dashboard use these directly. Agents should use the MCP tools instead.

Base URL: http://<host>:8000

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Liveness probe. Checks Fuseki, and Redis in ingest mode. Also reports the server mode and version.

Response

{"status": "ok", "mode": "ingest", "version": "0.2.0", "fuseki": true, "redis": true}

In serve mode redis is null. Returns 200 when healthy, 503 when degraded.

Serve mode

With CSQE_MODE=serve (read-only, Fuseki only) every endpoint below answers 503: there is no Redis or MinIO to back them. Only /health, /openapi.json and /mcp work.

docs.title: GET /status
docs.text:
Paginated list of all document pipeline states.

Query parameters

Parameter Default Description page 1 Page number (20 results per page)

Response

{
  "documents": [
    {
      "document_id": "eberron_3e",
      "title": "Eberron Campaign Setting (3.5e)",
      "status": "COMPLETED",
      "entity_count": 1247,
      "triple_count": 8931,
      "completed_at": "2026-06-21T14:32:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "page": 1
}

docs.title: GET /status/{document_id}
docs.text:
Full pipeline state for one document, including in-progress counters.

Response — in progress

{
  "document_id": "eberron_3e",
  "status": "EXTRACTING_ENTITIES",
  "current_chunk": 47,
  "total_chunks": 312
}

Response — failed

{
  "document_id": "eberron_3e",
  "status": "FAILED",
  "error": "LLM connection timeout",
  "last_successful_stage": "CLASSIFYING_SECTIONS"
}

docs.title: POST /ingest
docs.text:
Accept a PDF + metadata YAML and queue the document for processing.

Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Fields

Field Description pdf The PDF file metadata YAML string with document metadata

Metadata fields

Field Required Values document_id yes Unique slug (letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens) title yes Display name edition yes 3e, 4e, 5e, or any canon_type yes canon, kanon, or community publisher no Publisher name tags no List of strings

Example

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/ingest \
  -F "pdf=@eberron_campaign_setting.pdf" \
  -F 'metadata=document_id: eberron_3e
title: "Eberron Campaign Setting (3.5e)"
edition: 3e
canon_type: canon
publisher: "Wizards of the Coast"'

Response — 202 Accepted

{"document_id": "eberron_3e", "status": "PENDING"}

Error responses

Code Cause 409 document_id already exists 422 Missing or invalid fields 502 MinIO upload failure

docs.title: POST /admin/requeue/{document_id}
docs.text:
Reset a FAILED document back to PENDING. Only works when the document is in FAILED state.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/admin/requeue/eberron_3e

docs.title: POST /admin/restart/{document_id}
docs.text:
Force any document back to PENDING, releasing any stale lock. Works regardless of current state. Use this for documents stuck in an in-progress state (e.g. after a worker crash) or to re-trigger ingestion after a content update.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/admin/restart/eberron_3e

docs.title: Graph review
docs.text: These were MCP tools before 0.2.0. They read the graph-worker's Redis bookkeeping and are for operators auditing a run.

docs.title: GET /admin/type-assignments
docs.text:
Entity name → canonical type, as stored by the graph-worker.

Query parameter Default Description type_filter none Only entities assigned this class, e.g. Language limit 200 1–1000; anything else is a 400 
curl "http://localhost:8000/admin/type-assignments?type_filter=Language&limit=100"

{"assignments": [{"name": "Breland", "type": "Nation"}], "total": 1}

docs.title: GET /admin/type-conflicts
docs.text:
Entities classified as two unrelated types in different chunks; the first type was kept.

{"conflicts": [{"name": "Thrane", "existing_type": "Nation", "conflicting_type": "Language"}], "count": 1}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All configuration lives in config/ and is version-controlled. In Kubernetes, these files are mounted as a ConfigMap. In Docker Compose, they are volume-mounted read-only.

docs.title: LLM provider
docs.text:
File: config/llm.yaml

Configures the LiteLLM provider used by the graph-worker for entity extraction. All keys except model are passed directly to litellm.completion().

# llama.cpp / any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (default)
api_base: ${LLAMA_CPP_HOST}
model: openai/gemma4:e2b
api_key: dummy
timeout: 150

Swap providers by editing this file — no code changes needed:

OllamaMistral APIOpenAIAnthropic 
api_base: http://ollama:11434
model: ollama/gemma3:27b

api_base: https://api.mistral.ai
model: mistral/codestral-2501
api_key: ${MISTRAL_API_KEY}

model: gpt-4o
api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}

model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
api_key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}

Values matching ${VAR_NAME} are substituted from environment variables at startup. In Docker Compose set them in .env. In Kubernetes, inject them as env vars on the graph-worker pod.

max_tokens is controlled per-call by the pipeline (contextWindow / 4) and is not set here.

docs.title: Ontology schema
docs.text:
File: config/ontology_schema.yaml

Defines every entity type the pipeline can extract and how properties map to RDF triples. Adding a new entity type or a new property field requires only a YAML edit — no Python changes.

See Ontology for the full class and property reference.

docs.title: Ingestion parameters
docs.text:
File: config/ingestion_config.yaml

Controls chunking and extraction behaviour. The defaults are tuned for 8 192-token context windows.

docs.title: Fuseki dataset
docs.text:
File: config/fuseki-config.ttl

Apache Jena Fuseki Assembler configuration. Defines the TDB2 persistent dataset and enables tdb2:unionDefaultGraph so SPARQL queries see triples across all named graphs.

docs.text: Variable Default Description REDIS_URL redis://localhost:6379 Redis connection URL MINIO_ENDPOINT http://localhost:9000 MinIO endpoint MINIO_ACCESS_KEY minioadmin MinIO access key MINIO_SECRET_KEY minioadmin MinIO secret key INPUT_DIR /input Directory to watch for PDFs LOCK_TTL_SECONDS 120 Redis lock TTL per document POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS 5 Seconds between input directory polls LOG_LEVEL INFO Log level

docs.title: mcp-server
docs.text: Variable Default Description FUSEKI_ENDPOINT http://localhost:3030/campaign Fuseki SPARQL endpoint REDIS_URL redis://localhost:6379 Redis connection URL MINIO_ENDPOINT http://localhost:9000 MinIO endpoint MINIO_ACCESS_KEY minioadmin MinIO access key MINIO_SECRET_KEY minioadmin MinIO secret key ONTOLOGY_SCHEMA_PATH /config/ontology_schema.yaml Path to ontology schema LOG_LEVEL info Log level CSQE_MODE ingest ingest: full stack (Redis, MinIO, admin routes). serve: read-only, Fuseki only; admin routes answer 503. Any other value stops the server at startup MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS 12000 Upper bound on any MCP tool response, in characters. Set it to what your client model's context can take

docs.title: Docker Compose vs Kubernetes
docs.text:
In Docker Compose, LLAMA_CPP_HOST is the only variable you typically need to set — put it in .env and copy from .env.example.

In Kubernetes (Helm), use --set graphWorker.llamaCppHost=... or override llmConfig with a full provider config file. Passwords for Fuseki and MinIO are stored in Kubernetes Secrets and injected automatically.

docs.title: Helm Deployment
docs.text: The Helm chart deploys the full stack — mcp-server, pdf-worker, graph-worker, dashboard, Fuseki, Redis, and MinIO — to any Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Kubernetes 1.24+
  • Helm 3.8+
  • A Docker Hub account with the published images (or your own registry)
  • A default StorageClass that supports ReadWriteOnce PVCs (for Fuseki, Redis, MinIO)
  • A StorageClass supporting ReadWriteMany for the input and chunks volumes (NFS, EFS, CephFS, etc.)

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
helm install my-csqe oci://ghcr.io/sinan-ozel/charts/campaign-setting-query-engine \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --set image.organization=sinan-ozel \
  --set fuseki.adminPassword=changeme \
  --set minio.rootPassword=changeme

image.organization is the only required value — it is your Docker Hub username or org where the four images were published.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: All tunables live in values.yaml. Pass overrides with --set or -f my-values.yaml.

docs.title: Images
docs.text: Value Default Description image.registry docker.io Container registry image.organization (required) Docker Hub org or username image.tag chart appVersion Image tag; defaults to 0.1.0 image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Kubernetes pull policy

docs.title: Ingestion pipeline
docs.text: Value Default Description ingest.enabled true Deploy pdf-worker and graph-worker. Set false for a query-only stack (see Deploying on AWS with a GPU node)

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text: Value Default Description server.replicaCount 1 Number of replicas server.logLevel info Log level (debug, info, warning, error) server.resources {} CPU/memory requests and limits server.ingress.enabled false Enable Ingress server.ingress.host "" Hostname; blank defaults to mcp.<domain> when domain is set server.ingress.className / .annotations / .tls Same semantics as dashboard.ingress below

docs.title: PDF worker
docs.text: Value Default Description pdfWorker.replicaCount 1 Number of workers pdfWorker.logLevel info Log level pdfWorker.lockTtlSeconds 120 Redis lock TTL per document pdfWorker.pollIntervalSeconds 5 MinIO poll interval pdfWorker.resources {} CPU/memory requests and limits

docs.title: Graph worker
docs.text: Value Default Description graphWorker.replicaCount 1 Number of workers graphWorker.logLevel info Log level graphWorker.llamaCppHost http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1 LLM endpoint (override with your provider) graphWorker.contextWindow 8192 Token budget for chunking and LLM calls graphWorker.lockTtlSeconds 300 Redis lock TTL per document graphWorker.pollIntervalSeconds 10 MinIO poll interval graphWorker.resources {} CPU/memory requests and limits

docs.title: LLM server (GPU node)
docs.text:
Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp server, replacing an external graphWorker.llamaCppHost. Scheduled onto whichever node k3s-anywhere's GPU cloud-init labels k3s-anywhere.io/gpu-node=true.

Value Default Description llmServer.enabled false Deploy the in-cluster LLM server (and the NVIDIA device plugin DaemonSet) llmServer.image.repository / .tag sinanozel/llama.cuda / qwen3.5-9b-q4km Image with the model baked in — swap the tag to try a different model llmServer.port 8080 Container/service port llmServer.extraArgs [] Extra CLI args passed to the server llmServer.nodeSelector {k3s-anywhere.io/gpu-node: "true"} Where the LLM server (and device plugin) get scheduled llmServer.resources.limits {nvidia.com/gpu: 1} GPU allocation

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Value Default Description dashboard.replicaCount 1 Number of replicas dashboard.service.type ClusterIP Kubernetes service type dashboard.service.port 8501 Service port dashboard.ingress.enabled false Enable Ingress dashboard.ingress.host "" Hostname; blank defaults to domain when set dashboard.resources {} CPU/memory requests and limits

docs.title: MCP Inspector
docs.text:
Value Default Description inspector.enabled false Deploy the MCP Inspector, pointed at this release's mcp-server inspector.ingress.enabled false Enable Ingress inspector.ingress.host "" Hostname; blank defaults to inspector.<domain>

Auth is always on (no DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH — that's a local-docker-compose convenience only). Get the session token with: 

kubectl logs deploy/<release>-inspector

Staging by default; switch to https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory for a trusted cert on a long-lived deployment

docs.text: Value Default Description input.storage.size 100Gi PVC size for the PDF drop folder (ReadWriteMany) chunks.storage.size 50Gi PVC size for Markdown scratch space (ReadWriteMany)

docs.title: Config file overrides
docs.text:
The chart ships with default config files baked in. Override any of them with the full file content as a string value:

helm install my-csqe ... \
  --set-file llmConfig=my-llm.yaml \
  --set-file ontologySchema=my-ontology.yaml
Value Config file replaced fusekiConfig config/fuseki-config.ttl ontologySchema config/ontology_schema.yaml ingestionConfig config/ingestion_config.yaml llmConfig config/llm.yaml

docs.title: Using an external LLM
docs.text:
The graph-worker needs an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. Override graphWorker.llamaCppHost with your provider:

# Ollama running in the same cluster
--set graphWorker.llamaCppHost=http://ollama:11434

# OpenAI API (set model in llmConfig override)
--set graphWorker.llamaCppHost=https://api.openai.com/v1

For cloud providers (Mistral, Anthropic, OpenAI) you will also need to override llmConfig to set the correct model and API key env var substitution.

docs.title: Exposing the dashboard
docs.text:
Enable Ingress with a hostname:

dashboard:
  ingress:
    enabled: true
    className: nginx
    host: csqe.example.com
    annotations:
      cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt
    tls:
      - hosts: [csqe.example.com]
        secretName: csqe-tls

docs.title: Deploying on AWS with a GPU node
docs.text:
infrastructure/, deploy/, restore/, and .github/workflows/{provision,teardown,deploy,delete}.yaml stand up this chart on a k3s cluster provisioned by k3s-anywhere, with one GPU node running llmServer in place of an external LLM. Every step has a local .vscode/tasks.json task (k3s: ...) and a matching GitHub Actions workflow, so local testing and CI automation stay identical.

There's no external DNS — reachability is via the AWS Elastic IP through a nip.io hostname (<ip-with-dashes>.nip.io, which resolves any subdomain back to the embedded IP with no DNS records needed), so cert-manager can still issue real Let's Encrypt certs over HTTP-01 through Traefik (k3s's built-in ingress controller).

Rough order of operations (see each workflow/task for details):

  1. k3s: First-time setup (AWS) — once per AWS account.
  2. k3s: Provision (AWS) (or the provision.yaml workflow) — creates the cluster, including the GPU node.
  3. k3s: Deploy (or the deploy.yaml workflow) — restores any existing backup, installs cert-manager, computes the nip.io domain from the cluster's Elastic IP, and helm upgrade --installs this chart with llmServer.enabled=true, inspector.enabled=true, and Ingress enabled on all three of dashboard/mcp-server/inspector.
  4. k3s: Teardown (AWS) (or the teardown.yaml workflow) — backs up fuseki-data/redis-data/minio-data to S3, then destroys the cluster.

docs.title: Backups are versioned by major.minor
docs.text:
Every backup lands under a path for the release that took it (scripts/longhorn-backup-target.sh):

Version Longhorn backup target 0.1.x s3://<bucket>@<region>/ (bucket root, the backups from before versioning) 0.2.x and later s3://<bucket>@<region>/v<major>.<minor>/

Backup and restore both point Longhorn at the current version's path first. Within a major.minor, a new cluster resumes ingestion where the last backup left off: Redis comes back with the graph, so completed books aren't redone. After a minor bump (which every ontology change requires) the new path is empty, so the next deploy starts a fresh graph and the books are re-ingested. The older version's backups stay in the bucket untouched.

For a local, read-only copy see the serve mode in the quickstart: the k3s: Download Fuseki backup task writes backups/campaign_v<major>.<minor>_<timestamp>.nq.gz.

docs.title: Moving the finished graph to cheap infrastructure
docs.text:
No export/import file format — the same Longhorn backup taken at teardown (step 4 above) is the portability mechanism, since it snapshots redis-data right alongside fuseki-data (so ingestion-status/dedup/type state comes along with the graph, not just the TDB2 data). To run a finished graph on cheap CPU-only infrastructure once ingestion is done:

  1. Provision a second cluster with GPU_NODE_COUNT=0 pointed at the same STATE_BUCKET_NAME (so it shares the backup bucket).
  2. Run restore/ (k3s: Restore from backup task, or deploy.yaml's restore job) against it — this rehydrates the three PVCs from the last backup.
  3. helm upgrade --install with --set ingest.enabled=false --set llmServer.enabled=false — pdf-worker, graph-worker, and the GPU LLM server never get scheduled; Fuseki/mcp-server/dashboard come up already populated.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
helm upgrade my-csqe oci://ghcr.io/sinan-ozel/charts/campaign-setting-query-engine \
  --version 0.2.0 \
  -f my-values.yaml

Fuseki, Redis, and MinIO use ReadWriteOnce PVCs that survive upgrades. The knowledge graph is preserved across restarts.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
helm uninstall my-csqe

# Also delete PVCs (removes all graph data)
kubectl delete pvc -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=my-csqe

docs.title: MCP Tools
docs.text:
The server exposes 10 tools at the /mcp endpoint (streamable-http transport). Connect any MCP-compatible agent or client to http://<host>:8000/mcp.

The tools are built for small local models with small context windows (e.g. a 2B model with 32k context). They form a ladder, so that no single call can flood the client:

  1. Find names: list_names to enumerate a type, search_entities for a partial name.
  2. Follow links: get_relationships.
  3. Read one entity: get_entity.
  4. Cite: get_sources for books and pages.
  5. Fallback: search_text when no relationship or property fits.

describe_schema tells the model which types, relationships and properties exist.

Size limits. List tools page their results (limit / offset, at most 200 per page) and report total, truncated and next_offset. On top of that, every response is capped at MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS characters (default 12000, roughly 3k tokens). A response over the cap is trimmed and marked truncated: true with a note.

Errors come back as {"error", "did_you_mean", "hint"}. An unknown type, relationship or property gets its closest valid names; an unknown entity name gets the closest entity names.

docs.title: describe_schema
docs.text: What the graph can answer: entity types grouped under their root type, every relationship with a one-line meaning, filterable properties, enumerated values, and the workflow above. No input. Its output is a fixed ~2k tokens.

docs.title: list_names
docs.text:
Names of every entity of a type, alphabetical, one page at a time. Subtypes are included.

Field Type Default Description entity_type string required One of the entity types filters object {} Property → value, all must match; entity-valued properties match the linked entity's name edition string any 3e, 4e, 5e, any canon_type string any canon, kanon, community, any limit int 50 1–200 offset int 0 For paging 
list_names(entity_type="River")
→ {"entity_type": "River", "total": 23, "offset": 0, "count": 23, "names": ["Brey River", "Dagger River", ...]}

list_names(entity_type="Tradition", filters={"category": "fashion", "practicedBy": "Breland"})

docs.title: search_entities
docs.text:
Entities whose name or alias contains the query, best first (exact, then prefix, then substring; shorter names first).

Field Type Default Description query string required Part of a name or alias (2+ characters) entity_type string none Restrict to a type limit int 10 1–50 
search_entities(query="Cannith")
→ {"matches": [{"name": "House Cannith", "types": ["DragonmarkedHouse"]}, {"name": "Merrix d'Cannith", "types": ["NPC"]}, ...]}

docs.title: get_relationships
docs.text:
Entities reached from one entity over one relationship: names and types, paged.

Field Type Default Description entity_name string required Exact name or alias (case-insensitive) relationship string required e.g. members, capital, ruler, traditions, produces limit int 50 1–200 offset int 0 For paging 
get_relationships(entity_name="House Cannith", relationship="members")
get_relationships(entity_name="Breland", relationship="capital")   → Wroat

An empty result comes with a hint to read the entity's description or use search_text.

docs.title: get_location_hierarchy
docs.text:
Every place containing a location (nearest first), and the places inside it.

Field Type Default Description location string required Exact location name depth string direct direct: children only; all: every level below limit / offset int 50 / 0 Paging over children

docs.title: get_entity
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description name string required Exact name or alias (case-insensitive) section string facts facts or relationships page int 1 Page of relationships (60 links each)
  • facts: types plus every literal property (description, aliases, status, years, climate, ...).
  • relationships: every link to another entity, in both directions, grouped by relationship name.

When several entities carry the name, the one whose label matches exactly wins, and the rest are listed in other_matches.

docs.title: get_sources
docs.text:
Books (with edition and canonicity) and pages for up to 10 entities at once. Use it to cite answers.

get_sources(names=["Brey River"])
→ {"results": [{"name": "Brey River", "sources": [{"book": "Eberron: Rising from the Last War", "edition": "5e", "canon_type": "canon", "pages": ["142", "160"]}]}]}

docs.title: search_by_property
docs.text:
Names of entities of a type whose property matches a value.

Field Type Default Description entity_type string required Type to search in property_name string required One of the filterable properties value string required Case-insensitive match string exact exact or contains edition, canon_type, limit, offset As in list_names

docs.title: search_text
docs.text:
The fallback when no relationship or property fits: searches entity names and descriptions for the query's words, ranks entities by how many words they contain, and returns a snippet plus up to three sources for each.

Field Type Default Description query string required Words to look for (stopwords and words under 3 letters are ignored) entity_type string none Restrict to a type limit int 10 1–25 
search_text(query="capital of Breland")
→ {"matches": [{"name": "Wroat", "matched_words": 2, "snippet": "The capital of Breland.", "sources": ["Politics of Breland p.2", ...]}]}

docs.title: list_sources
docs.text: Every source book in the graph with edition, canonicity and the number of entities it mentions. No input.

docs.title: Moved out of MCP in 0.2.0
docs.text:
These were MCP tools before and are now admin HTTP endpoints, because they are for operators rather than client models (see Admin API):

Old tool Now get_ingestion_status GET /status, GET /status/{document_id} list_entity_type_assignments GET /admin/type-assignments list_type_conflicts GET /admin/type-conflicts list_completed_documents list_sources (reads the graph, works in serve mode) get_entity_edges get_entity(section="relationships") list_entities list_names + get_sources

docs.title: Ontology
docs.text:
Namespace: http://campaignsetting.io/ontology# (SPARQL prefix: cs:)

All entities extracted from sourcebooks live in this namespace. The graph is a standard RDF/SPARQL dataset hosted on Apache Jena Fuseki with TDB2 persistence. Everything on this page is generated from config/ontology_schema.yaml; the MCP tool describe_schema returns the same information to client models.

Changing the ontology

Any change to config/ontology_schema.yaml changes what the graph holds. It requires a minor version bump in server/__init__.py (CI enforces this) and a re-ingest. Backups are stored per major.minor, and serve mode only loads a backup of its own major.minor, so graphs built with different ontologies never mix. chart/files/ontology_schema.yaml must stay an exact copy (CI checks).

docs.title: Entity types
docs.text: Valid values for entity_type in list_names, search_entities, search_by_property and search_text. A type includes its subtypes: list_names(entity_type="Location") lists rivers, cities, mines, and so on.

docs.title: Characters and organisations
docs.text: Type Description NPC Named individuals with a proper name and established identity Faction Named organisations: guilds, crime families, military orders, spy agencies, newspapers, noble houses DragonmarkedHouse Dragonmarked houses (subtype of Faction) Newspaper Press organisations (subtype of Faction) Family Noble or criminal families (subtype of Faction)

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Type Description Religion Named religious systems and organised spiritual movements Deity Named divine beings, gods, and spiritual entities

docs.title: Species and mechanics
docs.text: Type Description Race Named biological species or ancestry types CharacterClass Named character classes, subclasses, archetypes, and prestige paths Skill Named discrete abilities, powers, or proficiencies Feat Named character-build options Creature Named creature species or individual monsters CreatureType Creature categories; subtypes Aberration, Beast, Celestial, Construct, Dragon, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, Giant, Humanoid, Monstrosity, Ooze, Plant, Undead

docs.title: Culture
docs.text: Type Description Language Named languages; subtypes Dialect, Creole, Pidgin, CodeLanguage (cants, ciphers, military codes) Tradition Cultural customs of a people: fashion, etiquette, law, dance, music, art, ritual, cuisine, festivals. category holds which Dish Named foods and culinary preparations (food only) Drink Named drinks; subtypes Wine, Beer, Spirit, Cocktail

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: Type Description Material Named raw materials; subtypes Metal, Gem, Textile, CraftingMaterial

docs.title: History
docs.text: Type Description Event Named historical events; subtypes War, Battle, Treaty, Disaster, Founding, Era (named ages such as the Age of Demons)

docs.title: Locations
docs.text: Type Description Location Base class; catch-all for named places Continent, Nation, Region Broad political and geographic areas City, Ward, Neighborhood Settlements and their districts Tavern Taverns, inns, pubs and breweries Restaurant Places whose business is serving meals Shop Places that sell products; shopType says which kind (blacksmith, florist, magic shop, tailor, spice shop, vendor stall, ...) Mine Named mines, quarries and digs Winery Named vineyards, wineries and distilleries (breweries are Taverns) River Flowing watercourses only Lake Inland bodies of still water Sea Seas, oceans, bays, gulfs, sounds and straits Mountain, MountainRange, Forest, Jungle, Desert, Plain, Island Terrain Dungeon, Ruin, Plane, Moon Structures and planes

docs.title: Items
docs.text: Type Description Item Base class for named items Attire Named clothing and worn accessories, magical or not Book Named books that exist inside the world (author and language linked) MagicItem Base class for magic items WondrousItem, MagicArmor, MagicWeapon, Potion, Ring, Rod, Scroll, Staff, Wand Magic item kinds

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Two simple fields, chosen so that a small extraction model gets them right:

  • status: current or past, on locations and languages. Destroyed places, former kingdoms such as Galifar or Cyre, and dead languages are past.
  • Years: fromYear / untilYear on locations and startYear / endYear on events, as integers in YK (Year of the Kingdom). Years before YK are negative. They are filled only when the text states the year outright: the model copies the number and never calculates one. A missing year means unknown, not current; status says whether something still holds.

Capitals and rulers carry their own current/former split: capitalStatus (current / former) on a city, and ruledBy / formerlyRuledBy on a nation or region.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Valid values for relationship in get_relationships. Each one reads in one direction; inverses have their own names (memberOf ↔ members).

Relationship Reads Meaning allies, enemies, sibling, spouse NPC → NPC Personal relationships memberOf / members NPC ↔ Faction Membership in factions, houses and families leaderOf / leader NPC ↔ Faction Leadership factionAllies, factionEnemies Faction → Faction Alliances and enmities between factions headquarters Faction → Location Headquarters memberFamilyOf / families Family ↔ DragonmarkedHouse House structure operatesIn Faction → Location Where a faction operates race, characterClass, nationality NPC → Race / Class / Nation Character facts locatedIn / residents NPC ↔ Location Where an NPC is usually found equipment NPC → Item Items carried worships / worshippers NPC, Faction ↔ Deity Worship primaryDeity, deityOf Religion ↔ Deity Pantheon structure contains / containedIn Location ↔ Location Direct spatial containment (use get_location_hierarchy for all levels) controlledBy / controls Location ↔ Faction Control capital, formerCapitals Nation → City Capital cities (derived, see below) capitalOf City → Nation The nation a city is or was capital of ruler, formerRulers / rules Nation, Region ↔ NPC Rulers now and in the past produces / producedAt Location ↔ Material, Drink What mines, wineries, breweries, regions and nations produce menu / servedIn Location ↔ Dish, Drink What a city, tavern or restaurant serves (also one-line menu boxes) localDishes / origin Location ↔ Dish A place's own dishes, and where a dish comes from (also when implied by its name) manifestZoneOf / manifestZones Location ↔ Plane Manifest zones participants / participatedIn Event ↔ NPC, Faction, Nation Who took part eventLocation / events Event ↔ Location Where it happened practicedBy / traditions Tradition ↔ Nation, Race, Faction Who practices a tradition spokenIn / languages Language ↔ Location Where a language is spoken spokenByRace, spokenByFaction Language → Race / Faction Who speaks it descendsFrom / descendants Language ↔ Language Language descent (creoles have several parents) dialectOf / dialects Dialect ↔ Language Dialects nativeRegions Race → Location Native regions author / wrote, writtenIn Book ↔ NPC, Book → Language In-game books foundIn / creatures Creature ↔ Location Habitats

Capitals are derived at query time. A city is a capital of a nation when it names the nation in capitalOf, or, when it names no nation, when it carries a capitalStatus and the nation is its nearest Nation ancestor in the containment hierarchy. capital returns current capitals and formerCapitals former ones.

Symmetric relationships (enemies, sibling, spouse, faction allies and enemies) are written in both directions at ingestion time.

docs.title: Filterable properties
docs.text:
Valid keys for filters in list_names and property_name in search_by_property. Literal properties match their value. Entity-valued properties (e.g. nationality, practicedBy) match the linked entity's name, so {"nationality": "Breland"} works.

Group Properties Shared description, alias, status, edition, canonType NPC nationality, alignment, ancestry, physicalDescription, level, wantsAndNeeds, worships, memberOf, leaderOf, locatedIn, hasRace, hasClass Faction factionType, dragonmark, factionLocatedIn, operatesIn Location climate, shopType, ambiance, controlledBy, capitalStatus, capitalOf, ruledBy, produces, manifestZoneOf, fromYear, untilYear Race, feat, food nativeRegion, prerequisites, cuisineType, originatesIn, servedIn, ingredient Items and books rarity, requiresAttunement, charges, author, writtenIn Language languageFamily, script, format, spokenIn, spokenByRace, descendsFrom, dialectOf Event, tradition startYear, endYear, occurredAt, participant, category, practicedBy Creature challengeRating, size, habitat, foundIn

Enumerated values: status = current / past; capitalStatus = current / former; Shop shopType = general store, blacksmith, armorer, weaponsmith, florist, magic shop, alchemist, apothecary, tailor, cobbler, jeweler, bookshop, spice shop, bakery, butcher, grocer, vendor stall, pawn shop, curio shop, other; Tradition category = fashion, etiquette, law, dance, music, art, ritual, cuisine, festival, other.

Scripts and language families are text fields, not entities, on purpose: many Eberron names are a language, a script and a family at once (Corvaguri, Siberine, Rhiavhaan), and entity identity is name-based.

docs.title: Source provenance
docs.text:
Every entity is linked to one or more cs:SourceBook nodes via cs:mentionedIn, and to cs:Mention nodes that pair a book with a page (cs:inBook, cs:atPage). Each source book carries:

  • rdfs:label: the book title
  • cs:edition: 3e, 4e, 5e, or any
  • cs:canonType: canon, kanon, or community

get_sources returns books and pages per entity. list_names, search_by_property and get_sources accept edition and canon_type filters.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: The only local requirement is Docker. No Python, no Node, no Fuseki installation needed.

docs.title: 1. Clone and configure
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/sinan-ozel/campaign-setting-query-engine.git
cd campaign-setting-query-engine
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and point it at your LLM:

LLAMA_CPP_HOST=http://your-gpu-host:8080/v1

The engine uses any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. See Configuration → LLM provider for Ollama, Mistral, and Anthropic examples.

docs.title: 2. Start the stack
docs.text:
docker compose up --build

Services start in dependency order. Fuseki takes ~30 seconds on first boot (TDB2 initialisation). When all services are healthy you'll see log lines from graph-worker polling for documents.

Service URL Dashboard http://localhost:8501 MCP server http://localhost:8000/mcp Fuseki admin http://localhost:3030 MinIO console http://localhost:9001

docs.title: 3. Ingest a sourcebook
docs.text:
Drop a PDF into the dashboard at http://localhost:8501, or use the API directly:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/ingest \
  -F "pdf=@eberron_campaign_setting_3e.pdf" \
  -F 'metadata=document_id: eberron_3e
title: "Eberron Campaign Setting (3.5e)"
edition: 3e
canon_type: canon
publisher: "Wizards of the Coast"
tags: [core-rulebook, setting-lore]'

The required metadata fields are:

Field Values document_id unique slug, e.g. eberron_3e title display name edition 3e, 4e, 5e, or any canon_type canon, kanon, or community

Poll for progress:

curl http://localhost:8000/status/eberron_3e

Pipeline states: PENDING → CONVERTING_PDF → MARKDOWN_READY → CLASSIFYING_SECTIONS → EXTRACTING_ENTITIES → MAPPING_TO_ONTOLOGY → LOADING_GRAPH → COMPLETED.

A large sourcebook (300+ pages) takes 30–90 minutes depending on LLM speed.

docs.title: 4. Connect your agent
docs.text:
Point any MCP client at http://localhost:8000/mcp. The server uses streamable-http transport (MCP standard).

Example — Claude Desktop claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "campaign-lore": {
      "transport": "streamable-http",
      "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp"
    }
  }
}

Your agent now has access to all 10 MCP tools. Try:

"List all rivers in Eberron from canon 3e sourcebooks."

"What is the capital of Breland?"

"List me d'Cannith family members."

"Tell me about fashion in Breland."

docs.title: Serve a finished graph (read-only)
docs.text:
Ingestion runs in the cloud with a GPU and a larger model. Once it's done, download the graph and serve it locally with no LLM, Redis, MinIO or workers. Your small client model talks to the MCP server; the server never calls an LLM.

  1. Download a backup with the k3s: Download Fuseki backup task. It writes backups/campaign_v<major>.<minor>_<timestamp>.nq.gz, with the version of the images that built the graph.

  2. Start serve mode:

    docker compose -f serve/docker-compose.yaml up --build

    A one-shot loader puts the newest campaign_v<major>.<minor>_*.nq.gz into an empty Fuseki, then the MCP server starts with CSQE_MODE=serve at http://localhost:8000/mcp. Set BACKUP_FILE=<name> to pick a specific backup.

  3. To switch to another backup, wipe the loaded graph first: docker compose -f serve/docker-compose.yaml down -v.

The loader only accepts a backup whose major.minor matches server/__init__.py. The MCP tools are built from the ontology, and a minor version bump means the ontology changed, so an older graph would answer questions with the wrong schema. Check out the release that matches your backup instead.

docs.title: Teardown
docs.text:
# Stop without losing data
docker compose down

# Stop and wipe all data (Fuseki graph, Redis state, MinIO objects)
docker compose down -v
